claims.text: Simple Jev uses compatible Hugging Face models to classify and score inputs, constructing JSON answers from next-token logits instead of generating a completion.

evidence.quote:
Use compatible open models from huggingface, for structured classification and scoring, without training a separate classifier head.

Explore the demos, playground, and documentation at [simple-jev.featherless.ai](https://simple-jev.featherless.ai/).

Send shared context and a set of questions. Simple Jev reads the model's next-token logits for each question and builds a JSON response containing choices, rubric scores, or truth/support judgments. The model does not generate a JSON completion: the server constructs the response from the scores.

The current implementation runs locally with Hugging Face Transformers and PyTorch. Shared request validation, versioned prompt instructions, and response scoring live in the plain Python `common/` folder so other inference implementations can use the same rules.

claims.text: It explores TypeSafe’s structured-decision interface with open models; it does not reproduce Jev’s architecture or training.

evidence.quote: The API takes inspiration from TypeSafe's structured-decision interface and includes project-specific behavior. `/v1/systemone` is an alias of `/v1/classifier`; both run the same implementation. Use this repository's [API reference](hf-server/API_REFERENCE.md) as the contract for clients. `GET /v1/models` advertises the served ID (`--served-model-name`, defaulting to `--model`). Request model IDs are unchecked unless `--enforce-model-id` is set. Choice defaults to a 255-option cap; set `--max-choice-options` to lower it. Formats for 50 or fewer choices are unchanged.

TypeSafe uses “System One” to describe models designed for fast, structured decisions, drawing the name from the distinction between fast intuitive thinking and slower deliberate reasoning. Its [introduction to System One and Jev](https://typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev) explains that motivation. Simple Jev explores this style of interface using existing open language models. It does not reproduce TypeSafe's model architecture or training, or establish equivalent accuracy, calibration, or speed.

claims.text: Send shared context as either state or messages, plus typed questions, to POST /v1/classifier on the configured server.

evidence.quote:
Send a non-streaming `POST /v1/classifier` request. With `--enforce-model-id`, the `model` value must exactly match the served ID. The examples below use Qwen; if you started Gemma, use `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` instead. Supply exactly one of:

- `state`: a string, JSON object, or JSON array containing the shared context.
- `messages`: text chat history, rendered using the model's own chat template.

The API takes inspiration from TypeSafe's structured-decision interface and includes project-specific behavior. `/v1/systemone` is an alias of `/v1/classifier`; both run the same implementation. Use this repository's [API reference](hf-server/API_REFERENCE.md) as the contract for clients. `GET /v1/models` advertises the served ID (`--served-model-name`, defaulting to `--model`). Request model IDs are unchecked unless `--enforce-model-id` is set. Choice defaults to a 255-option cap; set `--max-choice-options` to lower it. Formats for 50 or fewer choices are unchanged.

claims.text: Its choice and score confidence values are not calibrated correctness probabilities. Matching the response format establishes neither Jev-equivalent quality nor speed.

evidence.quote: Choice and score confidence is the largest probability among their allowed labels. These distributions, and the Noul value, are not calibrated probabilities of correctness.

TypeSafe uses “System One” to describe models designed for fast, structured decisions, drawing the name from the distinction between fast intuitive thinking and slower deliberate reasoning. Its [introduction to System One and Jev](https://typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev) explains that motivation. Simple Jev explores this style of interface using existing open language models. It does not reproduce TypeSafe's model architecture or training, or establish equivalent accuracy, calibration, or speed.

In this implementation, the useful change is how the model is used:

1. The shared prompt builder creates consistent classifier instructions and one scoring branch per question.
2. The HF server renders those instructions and the context into the model's native chat format.
3. It evaluates the exact common token prefix once and reuses that prefix's KV cache across batches of question suffixes.
4. It reads the next-token logits for the allowed answer labels. Shared scoring code normalizes those scores and constructs the JSON response.

This avoids generating and parsing a prose or JSON answer token by token. Reusing the context can also reduce repeated computation when several questions refer to the same input. Actual latency depends on the model, hardware, context length, and number of questions. Cache reuse currently lasts only for a single request.

A valid response structure does not guarantee a correct decision. Model capability and question wording still matter; evaluate answer quality on your own task separately from validating the server's inference and response pipeline.

sections.heading: Vai trò của Jev
sections.text: Dự án khám phá giao diện quyết định có cấu trúc của TypeSafe bằng mô hình mở, không tái tạo kiến trúc hay cách huấn luyện Jev.

sections.heading: Cách bắt đầu
sections.text: Gửi ngữ cảnh chung qua state hoặc messages, kèm câu hỏi có kiểu dữ liệu, đến POST /v1/classifier trên máy chủ đã cấu hình.

sections.heading: Phạm vi và giới hạn
sections.text: Độ tin cậy của choice và score không phải xác suất đúng đã hiệu chỉnh. Tương thích định dạng không chứng minh chất lượng hay tốc độ tương đương Jev.

tr.title: simple-jev — Açık modellerle kararlar
tr.h1: simple-jev — Açık model logits değerlerinden yapılandırılmış kararlar
tr.description: simple-jev: Açık Hugging Face modellerinin logits değerleriyle sınıflandırma ve puanlama; Jev’den esinlenen arayüz, bağımsız model uygulaması.
tr.summary: Simple Jev, uyumlu Hugging Face modelleriyle sınıflandırma ve puanlama yapar; metin üretmek yerine sonraki token’ın logits değerlerinden JSON yanıtı oluşturur. Ortak bağlamı state ya da messages alanlarından biriyle, türleri belirlenmiş sorularla birlikte sunucunun POST /v1/classifier uç noktasına gönderin.

sections.heading: Ne işe yarar
sections.text: Simple Jev, uyumlu Hugging Face modelleriyle sınıflandırma ve puanlama yapar; metin üretmek yerine sonraki token’ın logits değerlerinden JSON yanıtı oluşturur.

sections.heading: Jev’in rolü
sections.text: Açık modellerle TypeSafe’in yapılandırılmış karar arayüzünü araştırır; Jev’in mimarisini veya eğitimini yeniden üretmez.

sections.heading: Başlangıç
sections.text: Ortak bağlamı state ya da messages alanlarından biriyle, türleri belirlenmiş sorularla birlikte sunucunun POST /v1/classifier uç noktasına gönderin.

sections.heading: Kapsam ve sınırlar
sections.text: choice ve score güven değerleri, kalibre edilmiş doğruluk olasılıkları değildir. Aynı yanıt biçimi Jev’e eşdeğer kalite veya hızı kanıtlamaz.

it.title: simple-jev — Decisioni con modelli aperti
it.h1: simple-jev — Decisioni strutturate dai logits di modelli aperti
it.description: simple-jev: Classifica e valuta con logits di modelli aperti Hugging Face e un’interfaccia ispirata a Jev, senza riprodurne il modello.
it.summary: Simple Jev classifica e valuta con modelli Hugging Face compatibili, costruendo risposte JSON dai logits del token successivo senza generare una risposta testuale. Invia il contesto condiviso in state oppure messages, insieme a domande tipizzate, a POST /v1/classifier sul server configurato.

sections.heading: A cosa serve
sections.text: Simple Jev classifica e valuta con modelli Hugging Face compatibili, costruendo risposte JSON dai logits del token successivo senza generare una risposta testuale.

sections.heading: Ruolo di Jev
sections.text: Esplora l’interfaccia di decisioni strutturate di TypeSafe con modelli aperti; non riproduce l’architettura né l’addestramento di Jev.

sections.heading: Come iniziare
sections.text: Invia il contesto condiviso in state oppure messages, insieme a domande tipizzate, a POST /v1/classifier sul server configurato.

sections.heading: Ambito e limiti
sections.text: La confidenza di choice e score non è una probabilità calibrata di correttezza. La compatibilità del formato non dimostra qualità o velocità equivalenti a Jev.
